constraints: Eligibility thresholds and effective dates are authoritative outside the model.
The assistant should explain a result and expose uncertainty rather than invent a determination.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This division gives up automatic eligibility decisions, but it keeps the appealable calculation reproducible while preserving useful explanation.
details.errorCorrection: Keep the policy decision outside the model and validate the explanatory output; this reduces model flexibility but protects reproducibility and appeals.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A versioned rules service can evaluate dates and thresholds reproducibly, while the model receives structured results for explanation and citation.
details.scenarioApplication: The assistant can state the rule version, explain the returned inputs and outcome, and route missing or conflicting records to a caseworker.
details.transfer: The same boundary applies when a model summarizes a regulated calculation: computation and authorization remain in the system of record.

messages.text: Examples do not encode every threshold or effective-date rule and make the authority path unreproducible.
Prompted tables give context but do not provide a separately enforced calculation or guarantee that all rule conditions were applied.
Review after a disputed decision leaves the model as the initial authority and does not prevent an incorrect eligibility outcome.

feedback.reason: The deterministic service owns the consequence-bearing calculation; Claude performs the language work that benefits from context and can hand off an exception.

options.text: Ask Claude to infer the applicable threshold from examples and return the final eligibility decision as text.
Put the rule tables in the prompt and allow Claude to apply them without a separately validated calculation.
Have a rules service calculate eligibility, then give Claude the inputs and result to explain, cite, and route exceptions.

questions.prompt: A benefits assistant must explain eligibility while deterministic, versioned income and date rules remain authoritative. Which design puts Claude at the right boundary?

constraints: The request names an aspiration but no testable outcome.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Discovery and evaluation delay broad rollout, but they prevent optimization of a system whose value cannot yet be demonstrated.
details.errorCorrection: Do not treat interface polish, tool count, or subjective enthusiasm as the business requirement; define the behavior change and evidence first.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A baseline and representative test set turn a broad value word into a feedback loop for accuracy, time saved, handoff rate, and failure cases.
details.scenarioApplication: For scheduling, measure correctly proposed slots, time per appointment, and escalation across real case types against today's process.
details.transfer: Whenever a sponsor says productivity or transformation, ask what behavior changes, for whom, and how the current process will be compared.

messages.text: Usage and action completion can show activity but do not define a comparable scheduling outcome or establish whether the work became faster or better.
Model effort and favorable comments are proxies; neither supplies a task baseline or a reproducible quality criterion.
A cohort comparison without a defined task, baseline, or objective criteria can reflect novelty or workflow pressure rather than productivity.

feedback.reason: The team cannot diagnose a productivity effect until it defines the work unit and compares it with current practice. A task-specific evaluation should precede prompt or architecture changes.

options.text: Define a scheduling task, measurable success criteria, representative cases, and a baseline before tuning the prompt or architecture.
Instrument the prototype and run a limited pilot using usage and action completion as initial indicators while leaving the current process unmeasured.
Increase model effort and choose the version that receives the most favorable reviewer comments.
Roll the prototype to a representative scheduler cohort and compare self-reported usefulness and usage before defining a formal productivity baseline.

questions.prompt: A hospital scheduling team asks for a Claude assistant to “improve productivity.” The prototype has a polished chat screen, reviewers disagree about usefulness, and there is no current-process baseline. What should the architect do next?

constraints: All required inputs are structured and the validated rules service meets the 40 ms p95 target.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The design gives up speculative model coverage but protects a proven latency and correctness path and avoids redundant spend.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Structured validation is already handled by ordinary code; Claude becomes useful only where unstructured interpretation or explanation creates measured value.
details.scenarioApplication: Keep the 40 ms rules path, monitor correctness and exception volume, and separately test Claude on a concrete explanation or investigation workload if one exists.
details.transfer: Before adding an LLM, ask whether every input and decision rule are already deterministic and whether any language task has measurable value.

messages.text: An advisory second classifier still adds a redundant language path when no measured language task is missing; disagreement data does not establish a defined explanation need.
Replacing a deterministic validator with a language model weakens reproducibility and makes post-posting review the safety net.
Sampling every record still adds cost and does not identify a missing language task or an acceptance criterion.

feedback.reason: Introducing a model adds latency and an unmeasured failure mode without a language-shaped problem to solve. The existing deterministic path should remain canonical while evidence guides any later language capability.

options.text: Run an advisory Claude classifier alongside the rules service, compare disagreements, and keep the deterministic result authoritative.
Keep the deterministic service in the posting path, measure its correctness and exceptions, and reserve Claude for an evidenced unstructured explanation task.
Replace the rules service with Claude and recover disagreements through manual review after posting.
Send a sample of every record to Claude first, then choose the route from whichever result appears more descriptive.

questions.prompt: A utility billing service receives 200,000 normalized records per day. A deterministic rules service already validates them in 40 ms p95, and all required fields are structured. The team proposes adding Claude to classify each record before posting. Which decision is best?

constraints: The alert deadline is 100 ms p95 and the immediate alert uses structured event codes.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Use synchronous Claude only if a paired benchmark shows completion and freshness fit the 100 ms contract; otherwise retain the asynchronous boundary.
details.errorCorrection: The split path adds coordination and a stale-result state, but it preserves both the operational deadline and the measured business value of narrative analysis.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A synchronous structured alert preserves the hard SLA; an asynchronous Claude job can analyze the immutable snapshot and attach provenance so commanders know what evidence it used.
details.scenarioApplication: Publish the code-derived alert at once, queue the narrative with snapshot version and completion time, and show it as supplemental until a commander reviews it.
details.transfer: When a language result is valuable but misses a hard deadline, isolate it behind a versioned asynchronous contract instead of weakening the deadline.

messages.text: Negotiating away the stated deadline makes the slower narrative the gate and breaks the existing alert contract.
Without the immutable snapshot version and freshness marker, a later narrative can describe a different incident state and cannot be safely joined to the alert.
First-token latency is not a complete validated alert; streaming partial narrative text leaves the required decision and evidence unfinished.

feedback.reason: The value-bearing narrative is real but its measured latency cannot satisfy the immediate alert contract. Separate the deterministic deadline path from an asynchronous, freshness-labeled language result.

options.text: Put Claude in the synchronous alert path and negotiate a longer deadline so its narrative can accompany the alert.
Emit the deterministic alert within the deadline, then run Claude asynchronously on the immutable snapshot and attach its versioned narrative for commander review.
Compute a synchronous deterministic alert and attach an asynchronous Claude narrative from current logs, but omit the incident snapshot version and freshness marker.
Stream Claude's first narrative tokens into the alert dashboard so operators see useful text within 100 ms while final validation continues.

questions.prompt: A warehouse alert service must emit a structured alert within 100 ms p95 from event codes. constraints: Free text is the only ambiguous input; normalized codes already meet the latency target.

Notes can be labeled for a bounded held-out evaluation.

messages.text: This preserves deterministic authority but leaves the measured unstructured bottleneck unsolved even though a bounded extraction experiment is available.

feedback.reason: The business need now includes an evidenced unstructured extraction step, so a narrowly augmented model adds value without replacing the proven decision service.

Keep the rules-only path and send every note-bearing record to manual entry until upstream codes cover the fault.

Use a keyword and regular-expression parser for notes and post its normalized fields directly, reserving manual review only for parser errors.

questions.prompt:

Which architecture addresses the note bottleneck while preserving the posting authority?

details.transfer: Use measured evidence and the stated authority boundary to choose the least complex design that satisfies the workload's constraint; revisit the route when the counterfactual changes.

messages.text: Chat is unavailable in the operating process, and the higher correction rate means the local gain may increase total work rather than improve the business outcome.

Throughput alone omits the required handling-time and completed-appointment quality measures and does not test whether structured extraction can reduce the actual bottleneck.

feedback.reason: The decision fits the actual work surface and prevents a local summarization gain from being mistaken for business value.

options.text: Launch a conversational assistant because first-review time improved and let staff adapt their workflow around it.
Pilot a structured queue extractor that flags missing fields, leaves scheduling to staff, and expand only if end-to-end outcomes improve.
Keep the queue surface but expand the summarizer solely because first review fell from 6.0 to 4.5 minutes; treat the extra corrections as normal staff work.
Leave the current manual queue unchanged and measure only forms completed per hour until the correction rate returns to baseline.

questions.prompt:

Which next step translates this request into a safe, measurable workflow and value decision?

constraints: Triage speed is the measured outcome.
Equipment switching remains outside Claude's authority.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The bounded design leaves switching with existing controls, which limits immediate automation but reduces operational risk while the team learns where autonomy is justified.
details.errorCorrection: State the business result, authority limit, and acceptance evidence before selecting a model pattern or implementation investment.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A bounded extraction, retrieval, and drafting workflow can expose structured fields, preserve an operator handoff, and feed measured outcomes back into design.
details.scenarioApplication: The utility can compare minutes per incident, severity accuracy, and escalation rate with the current process before expanding capability.
details.transfer: Use the same framing for claims or support: name the work unit to improve, the authority the system has, and the evidence that will show improvement.

messages.text: Usage and feedback from a general chat pilot do not establish the triage outcome, authority boundary, or a reproducible acceptance test.
A confidence threshold does not authorize a consequential equipment action and would cross the explicit switching boundary.
Training investment and an informal interim signal precede definition of the work, handoff, and success test, so the implementation choice substitutes for problem framing.

feedback.reason: The scope starts with the measurable triage job and makes the authority boundary executable. It gives the team an observable first release instead of treating more autonomy or more training as the business requirement.

options.text: Start with a general operator chat pilot, collect usage and feedback, and defer a formal triage measure until the pilot reveals which workflow matters.
Build a bounded workflow that extracts location and severity, retrieves the runbook, drafts a triage summary, routes uncertainty to an operator, and measures time and classification quality.
Let an agent choose and execute switching commands whenever its outage classification confidence exceeds the launch threshold.
Fine-tune on historical outage emails first, use existing analyst judgments as an interim signal, and define the triage handoff after the model stabilizes.

questions.prompt: A regional utility receives 18,000 free-form outage emails each day. Operations wants to cut triage time to 15 minutes per incident, while equipment switching remains outside the model's authority. Which initial solution best translates the business problem into a production scope?

constraints: The release should target policy lookup time and recommendation quality.
Refund authorization remains with a supervisor.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A narrower release defers refund automation but lowers exposure and produces evidence for the next investment.
details.errorCorrection: Translate automation into a target work step and an authority statement before broadening data or permissions.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Retrieval and structured drafting can reduce policy-search effort; a baseline and supervisor outcomes close the business feedback loop.
details.scenarioApplication: Pilot representative returns, compare minutes per case, inspect policy support, and record which recommendations supervisors accept or correct.
details.transfer: For any operational assistant, pair a value measure with what the model may prepare and what a person or deterministic service must decide.

messages.text: Throughput and handling time measure speed, but deferring policy grounding and supervisor acceptance to a later review omits the release evidence required for a usable recommendation.

Unbounded ingestion adds cost and complexity without testing the measured policy-lookup bottleneck.
Without b, the team cannot demonstrate whether the workflow reduces handling time or improves recommendations.

feedback.reason: The first release pairs the measured bottleneck with an observable workflow and preserves the supervisor's consequential decision. Both value evidence and responsibility are explicit.

options.text: Measure message throughput and handling time for the workflow, then capture policy grounding and supervisor acceptance in a later review.

Give Claude permission to approve refunds after it retrieves a policy passage.
Use Claude to summarize the case, retrieve the applicable policy, and draft a recommendation while the supervisor decides.
Index every internal data source before measuring whether policy retrieval is the returns bottleneck.

Store staff read customer messages, check policy, and prepare a recommendation; a time study shows policy lookup consumes most handling time, and a supervisor retains refund authorization. Which TWO decisions best translate this problem into a coherent first release? Select TWO.

constraints: The output shape is valid but the missed decision is not attributable.
Lawyer outcomes and source document versions are available to capture in a revised design.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: More structured logging and labeling costs storage and review time, but it prevents blind prompt changes and makes improvement attributable.
details.errorCorrection: Separate transport or schema success from task success and capture the evidence required to locate the failing stage.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Versioned inputs and configuration plus evidence and reviewer outcomes turn a final response into a diagnosable execution record and a reproducible evaluation slice.
details.scenarioApplication: Join each missed renewal clause to its document revision, retrieved passage, prompt release, lawyer correction, and eventual case outcome before comparing fixes.
details.transfer: When a system appears correct syntactically but fails business decisions, add stage-level provenance and outcome labels before changing the model.

messages.text: More model effort cannot reveal which source or release caused a miss when the service has discarded the relevant provenance.
Tool count and JSON validity do not measure renewal recall or identify whether retrieved evidence supported the decision.
A labeled monthly recall sample is better than raw counts, but an aggregate monthly result cannot attribute misses to a document, revision, or prompt release.

feedback.reason: Valid JSON only proves serialization. The missing links prevent the team from determining whether the defect came from source version, retrieval, prompt behavior, or review, so traceable outcome data is the first diagnosis.

options.text: Record document and policy versions, prompt release, retrieved evidence, lawyer accept/edit/reject outcome, and link those fields to held-out evaluation cases.
Increase model effort and inspect a few fluent summaries without changing the event data captured by the service.
Add every contract repository as a tool and treat the resulting JSON validity rate as the quality measure.
Compare monthly renewal-clause recall on a labeled sample and tune the highest-recall prompt, then track the aggregate result by month.

questions.prompt: A contract review service logs valid JSON output but still misses renewal clauses. The logs cannot identify the document revision, prompt release, or lawyer outcome associated with each miss. What should the architect diagnose first?

constraints: A timeout does not reveal whether the refund committed.
The provider contract includes a request identity and status lookup that the application can use.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The extra lookup and state handling increase integration complexity, but they prevent duplicate refunds and support an auditable recovery path.
details.errorCorrection: Treat side-effect uncertainty as a state-machine problem with an external source of truth, not as a text classification problem.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A durable request record plus provider idempotency and status lookup separates transport uncertainty from the external financial state; Claude may explain the state but does not guarantee it.
details.scenarioApplication: Store the request before submission, record the provider response or timeout, check status by request ID, and send only genuinely unresolved cases to operations.
details.transfer: Use the same pattern for any provider operation whose commit may precede the response: identity, durable intent, reconciliation, and explicit unknown.

messages.text: A new identity can create a second refund after the first request committed, and success of the last call does not prove the first state.

Message and error text cannot establish provider-side financial state or safely decide whether to repeat a side effect.

details.errorCorrection: Do not collapse delayed outcomes into contemporaneous volume or satisfaction metrics; preserve the causal identifiers before deployment changes.

details.scenarioApplication: For every claim, store the recommendation release, policy revision, adjuster action, and later resolution or recontact outcome, then compare matched cohorts.
details.transfer: For recommendations whose success appears later, define the outcome event and immutable decision lineage before claiming a model improvement.

messages.text: Aggregate volume and satisfaction cannot separate releases or show whether a specific recommendation led to the later outcome.
Re-running with today's prompt answers a different question and cannot replace the production decision and context that preceded the outcome.
Memory-based quarterly impressions are neither complete nor attributable to a release or case.

feedback.reason: Delayed outcomes only become useful feedback when they remain joined to the decision context that produced them. Version and reviewer identifiers prevent later releases from being mistaken for the original cause.

options.text: Correlate each recommendation with the case, source and policy versions, prompt/model release, reviewer action, and later resolution outcome before comparing versions.
Compare weekly recommendation volume and customer satisfaction without retaining which release produced each case.
Use the latest prompt to re-run old cases and treat its offline score as the production outcome regardless of the historical decision.
Ask reviewers to remember difficult cases and report a qualitative view at the end of each quarter.

questions.prompt: A claims recommender is judged by customer resolution that may arrive weeks after the recommendation. The service has multiple prompt and policy releases during that period. Which feedback-loop design yields attributable evidence?

constraints: The downstream service requires a typed payload and complete business fields.

details.errorCorrection: Place deterministic validation immediately before the external side effect and make the failure state observable instead of filling gaps silently.

details.scenarioApplication: Reject malformed JSON, flag missing fields and invalid values, preserve the source and model response for correction, and post only validated records.
details.transfer: Use separate parse, field-completeness, business-rule, and authorization checks whenever an AI output drives a typed external operation.

messages.text: A prompt request does not validate the application payload or prevent an invalid response from reaching the ERP.
Refusal is not the only failure mode; parseable objects can still omit required fields or violate business rules.
Defaults can create false business data and turn missing evidence into an external mutation.

feedback.reason: Serialization and business validity are separate gates. A typed validator and quarantine keep malformed or incomplete model output from becoming an external ERP mutation.

options.text: Ask Claude in the system prompt to be more careful and post the next response if it parses as JSON.
Have a reviewer inspect only records that produce a model refusal while all parseable objects post automatically.
Wrap any missing field with a default value and send the record onward so the ERP queue remains full.
Parse against a typed schema, validate required fields and business rules, quarantine failures with evidence, and require correction or review before posting.

questions.prompt: An ERP posting workflow receives Claude's extraction, but malformed JSON and missing required fields occasionally reach the posting service. Which architecture should stop the defect at the correct boundary?

constraints: The gateway contract proves no provider call occurred and no provider request ID exists.

messages.text: That discards the gateway contract that proves no provider call occurred and can leave a valid refund unnecessarily unresolved.

options.text: Treat every failure as an unknown side effect and wait for reconciliation before attempting any retry.

Record the rejection and retry once with the same key after current checks; reconcile any subsequent unknown outcome.

constraints: Claude may prepare the request and citations, but the closure mutation is irreversible.

details.scenarioApplication: Persist the request and evidence, run identity and retention checks, obtain the officer confirmation at the checkpoint, execute once through the closure service, and record the result.

messages.text: A citation does not prove current authorization and post-action notification cannot prevent an irreversible closure.

options.text: Let Claude close the account after it cites the retention policy, then notify compliance in the audit report.

questions.prompt:

constraints: The pipeline must validate and enrich before assignment.

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The explicit stages add persistence and integration work, but they make failures diagnosable and prevent a polished response from being mistaken for an effective claims process.
details.errorCorrection: Do not stop at a model response or UI demo; connect each production handoff and feedback signal before selecting the implementation.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Validation creates an admissible input contract, retrieval supplies policy context, structured model output supports routing, and review plus outcome records make later evaluation attributable.

messages.text: Direct generation skips input validation and loses the correction data needed to measure whether the queue recommendation helps.

options.text: Send the raw claim directly to Claude, display its queue suggestion, and let adjusters correct problems without recording the corrections.

questions.prompt: An insurer needs claim text validated, enriched with policy context, assigned to a queue, reviewed by an adjuster, and evaluated from the eventual outcome. Which architecture best makes that end-to-end loop explicit?

constraints: The external hold may have committed even when the caller times out.

constraints: The handbook fits in the selected model's context.
